The distribution of the RNA expression data (COAD, data/COAD__geneExp.xls, 20,502 genes x 328 samples) is HIGHLY RIGHT-SKEWED (positively skewed) on the raw, as-delivered expression scale.

Supporting evidence (script analyze_skewness.py, executed):
- Pooled distribution (all genes x samples, n=6,724,656): skewness coefficient (Fisher–Pearson, bias-corrected) = 42.44; mean 932.0 vs median 176.8 vs max 1,336,107 — mass concentrated near zero with a very long right tail. By Bulmer's rule (|skew|>1 => highly skewed; + => right), this is classified as highly right-skewed.
- Per-gene skewness across samples (20,026 genes after excluding 476 zero-variance genes): median = 2.03, mean = 3.63; 99.8% of genes are right-skewed, 80.3% are highly right-skewed (skew > 1), only 4.1% |skew|<0.5.
- Per-sample skewness across genes: median 20.63 (range 11.5–110.8), 100% of samples right-skewed.
- Robustness (tumor-only '01', n=285): pooled skewness 36.00 — still highly right-skewed.
- Sensitivity only (not the headline scale): log2(x+1) pooled skewness = −0.30 (approximately symmetric, mildly left); this confirms the raw distribution is the unlogged, strongly right-skewed one.
- Normality tests (note only): D'Agostino stat 3.03e6; Shapiro-Wilk stat 0.24 (p<1e-10) — trivial rejection at n≈6.7M; verdict based on skewness effect size and shape, not p-value.
- Diagnostics saved: figure_1_raw_hist.svg (raw histogram), figure_3_per_gene_skew.svg (per-gene skewness), figure_2/4 (log2 sensitivity hist + QQ).

Final classification: highly right-skewed (positive).
